title: A Sugar Cube of This Star Weighs a Billion Tons

scenes.text: A sugar cube of this star would weigh a billion tons.
It's called a neutron star, and it's what's left behind when a giant star explodes.
It packs up to twice the mass of our Sun into a ball the size of a city.
NASA puts it this way: one sugar cube of it weighs about as much as a mountain.
Some of them spin faster than a kitchen blender. The fastest known turns forty-three thousand times a minute.
It happens because gravity crushes the atoms until protons and electrons merge into neutrons, with no empty space left.
Would you rather fly past a black hole or a neutron star?

description:
A sugar cube of neutron star material would weigh about a billion tons on Earth, as much as a mountain.
A neutron star is the collapsed core left after a giant star explodes. It squeezes up to twice the Sun's mass into a ball the size of a city.
The fastest known one spins 43,000 times a minute, faster than a kitchen blender.
Would you rather fly past a black hole or a neutron star?
